summary.text: A 57-year-old man with alcohol-related decompensated chronic liver disease and portal hypertension, with an upper gastrointestinal bleed that required endoscopic variceal ligation, a seizure episode one year earlier, hypertension, hypothyroidism on oral thyroxine and vitiligo, was hospitalized for living donor liver transplantation. Admission vital signs were normal, examination showed signs of jaundice, the MELD score was 23 and the autoimmune panel was positive for ANA and ANCA.

He underwent living donor liver transplantation with a right lobe graft from his 19-year-old daughter, lasting 7.5 hours. Intra-operative bleeding was treated with packed red cells, fresh-frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate and tranexamic acid. He was extubated the same day and received piperacillin-tazobactam, teicoplanin, fluconazole, methylprednisolone, albumin, electrolyte replacement and furosemide.

On postoperative day 6 he began passing 7-8 L of urine per day without diuretics, with ADH 73 pg/mL, serum osmolality 255 mOsm/kg, urine specific gravity 1.015 and normal serum sodium. A brain MRI done to rule out central DI showed a normal pituitary with age-related involutional changes, mild small vessel ischemic disease and chronic lacunar infarcts. The authors diagnosed diabetes insipidus, thought to be nephrogenic and idiopathic.

He was started on desmopressin nasal spray twice daily, changed after two days to oral tablets twice daily, and stopped after five days on POD 10; he responded well and was discharged on POD 17. After discharge he remained asymptomatic without recurrence of polyuria or polydipsia, with normal routine laboratory work, and reported complete remission of his polyuria and polydipsia. He reported satisfaction with his quality of life and fully resumed daily activities.

article_limitations: Figure 1 and Tables 1 to 4 are referenced only as "see PDF": the source declares no figure, table or supplement assets, so they are unavailable media under MEDIA-UNAVAILABLE (complete, flagged; media_available=false, content_reviewed=false). Their contents (Figure 1, pre-operative and post-operative laboratory values, anesthesia protocol, literature case table) were not viewed and are not annotated.
Two published central DI cases in the Discussion are cited literature and are not assigned to the index patient.

Urine osmolality (405 mOsm/kg) is called normal in the case report and high in the sentence confirming the diagnosis; the value is accepted and only the normal/high classification is review-only source conflict.

Brain MRI is described as showing no abnormality in several places while the findings paragraph lists involutional changes, small vessel disease and lacunar infarcts; unscoped statements are review-only.
The sentence about antibiotics places "intravenous" only before piperacillin-tazobactam, so no route is assigned to teicoplanin or fluconazole.
Whether endoscopic variceal ligation was completed is not stated (the bleed "required" it).
Blood pressure and heart rate on POD 6 are stated in a separate sentence without a time of their own; time left null.
